summary.text: Matt Van Epps is a West Point graduate and Army aviator who served ten years on active duty, then worked in business and in Tennessee state government under Gov. Bill Lee, including as Commissioner of General Services. He won the 2025 special election to succeed Rep. Mark Green and is running for a full term supporting President Trump's agenda.

paragraphs.text: Van Epps was born March 29, 1983, and, according to Wikipedia, graduated from Mentor High School in Mentor, Ohio.

He graduated from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 2005 with a bachelor's degree in political science and mechanical engineering, and later earned a Master of Public Administration from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

He served ten years on active duty as an Army aviator, deploying to Iraq and Afghanistan and flying AH-64D Apache and MH-47G Chinook missions with the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment as a pilot-in-command and air mission commander. He continued to serve in the Tennessee Army National Guard, rising to Lieutenant Colonel.

After active duty, Van Epps served as senior vice president of operations at Main Street Health, a start-up focused on value-based rural healthcare, and worked as a consultant. Ballotpedia also lists him as founder of the consulting firm Darkhorse Strategy, LLC.

In Gov. Bill Lee's administration he was assistant commissioner at the Tennessee Department of Veterans Services, assistant director of procurement and contracts at the Department of Transportation, a strategic planner with the COVID-19 Unified Command Group, and Deputy Chief Operating Officer in the Governor's Office. He also served on the Tennessee Higher Education Commission.

Gov. Lee named him Commissioner of the Tennessee Department of General Services effective October 1, 2024, overseeing statewide procurement, real estate, and facilities operations. He stepped down on June 10, 2025 to pursue a new venture.

Van Epps won the October 7, 2025 Republican primary for the vacant 7th District seat with 51.6% of the vote in an 11-candidate field. He then defeated Democrat Aftyn Behn in the December 2, 2025 special election, 53.9% to 45.1%, and was sworn in on December 4, 2025. He was renominated unopposed in the August 6, 2026 primary.
In the House he serves on the Committee on Homeland Security, including its Subcommittee on Transportation and Maritime Security, and on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
According to his official House biography, he lives in Nashville with his wife and child.
